newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures fall near lower end of ranges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures fall near lower end of ranges.

text.p: U.S. debt futures fell near the lower end of their 2-1/2-week ranges in light profit-taking due to growing concerns about Tuesday's fourth-quarter U.S. employment cost index, traders and analysts said.
"There are big concerns about the index," one Eurodollar futures trader said.

He said weakness in the U.S. bond pit spilled into the Eurodollars market, pushing June Eurodollars through support at 94.17 and keeping the September contract below the 94.02 support level. Further support is seen at 94.15 and 94.13 for June and 93.94 for September.
"March bonds broke through 110-16/32, which was seen as a pivotal area," another Eurodollar trader said. "It looks like the contract will test 109-26/32."
The 109-26/32 level is the January 10 low, which represents the lower end of March bond's 2-1/2-week low.
However, several bond futures traders said March T-bonds could find support at 110-08/32 to 110-09/32, and possibly firm in the afternoon.
Some said the expiration of February bond options at 1200 CST/1800 GMT would lead the March T-bond futures contract back towards the 111-00 level.
Others noted that bond futures were staging a decent performance on early Friday, even though the contracts were lower.
They said profit-taking pressure was mild considering the steep drop in U.S. stocks late Thursday and given concerns about next week's employment cost index.

"One should expect some pressure in the market," William Bohnsack, president of W.H. Bohnsack & Co, said. "If these levels hold, I would look for an effort to test upper resistance and possibly 112-00 to 113-00."
Bohnsack also said the firm tone in the overseas bond markets was containing losses in bonds.
However, he said the trend in Eurodollars was not as positive as bonds.
"I'd like to see the short-term leading the front end, but it's not leading," Bohnsack. "It's not even confirming the short-term trend in bonds."
"You can't have a real strong trend in bonds without the Eurodollars confirming," he added.
He said Eurodollars were pricing in fears of an interest rate hike.

At 0835 CST/1435 GMT, March T-bonds were down 08/32 at 110-19/32, June and September Eurodollars were each down two bps at 94.17 and 93.99, respectively, and June T-bills were one bps lower at 94.74. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
